briefing.headline: Dry and sunny Saturday. Mild Sunday, near 60° for the 1 PM kickoff, with about a 40% chance of showers during the game. Rain is most likely Sunday evening and night.

sections.title: Saturday
sections.text: **Sunny and dry.** Low to mid 40s at 7 AM, rising to the low 60s by mid-afternoon with light wind. Sunset is at 4:41 PM; temperatures fall into the 50s soon after and the upper 40s by late evening.

sections.title: Sunday
sections.text: **Cloudy and mild,** near 60° from 1 to 4:30 PM with a light breeze. Chance of rain in that window: about 40%. Chance of a soaking (0.25 in or more): about 15%. Rain becomes more likely after 4:30 PM, about a 50% chance Sunday evening and night. Most forecasts total under 0.25 in; the wettest exceed 1 in. No snow or thunder is expected.

sections.title: Monday morning
sections.text: Any rain ends early. Temperatures in the 50s; a few forecasts turn breezy, with gusts near 25 mph by late morning.

sections.title: What to bring
sections.text: **Saturday:** a jacket or fleece early, long sleeves for the afternoon, and sunglasses for the low sun. **Sunday:** long sleeves, a light jacket and a hooded rain jacket or poncho (many stadiums do not allow umbrellas in the seats), plus water-resistant shoes. **Monday:** a wind-resistant jacket.

briefing.confidence: **Saturday: high.** **Sunday afternoon and night: low.** Rain depends on the track of a low moving up the coast; forecasts should converge by Thursday. Next update: Thursday morning.
briefing.fans:
High pressure covers the Mid-Atlantic on Saturday. A low forms off the Southeast coast and moves north Sunday ahead of a Great Lakes cold front. The latest runs split on its rain shield: GFS brings about 1.8 in to Philadelphia by Monday midday, NBM about 0.4 in, and the ECMWF IFS stays dry.

Over the event, the ensembles give a 51–71% chance of measurable rain and a 35–59% chance of 0.25 in or more. ECMWF ENS is driest and AIFS ENS wettest. For the game window (1–4:30 PM) the three systems give 29%, 35% and 53%.
